text:
marcus: quick q — when a request gets routed hosted -> private, who stamps policy labels (quota, tier, customer_id)?

sophia: control-plane should stamp before routing so telemetry keeps provenance. avoids copying label logic into every runtime. :+1:

priya: that helps but private runtimes sometimes need to augment or tighten policies (local contracts). how do we avoid double-billing or conflicting labels?

ben: two approaches: (1) control-plane pre-label + X-Policy-Source=controlplane header; runtime can only append but not override, rejecting on conflict. (2) runtime is authoritative for final labels and returns a label-delta for billing. (1) is easier for routing semantics.

marcus: i'm leaning (1). control-plane-driven routing is simpler. requirement: private/runtime rejects must map to clear, machine-parsable errors so control-plane can surface to caller.

priya: agree. also require immutable audit fields preserved: X-Customer-ID and X-Request-UUID. if runtime modifies, it must return a signed assertion.

ben: sketch of headers control-plane will inject:

```
X-Customer-ID: cust_42
X-Request-UUID: d4f3c1a2
X-Policy-Source: controlplane
X-Policy-Signature: sig_v1(base64)
```

sophia: signature is required for tamper detection on private/on-prem. key distribution question: long-lived tenant keys vs ephemeral mTLS certs?

marcus: proposal: short-lived mTLS certs (48h) provisioned by control-plane CA. enterprise customers can enable HSM-bound certs. control-plane rotates and pushes certs at provisioning time.

priya: fallback behavior: if cert push fails, runtime can accept a transient allowlist mode but must mark telemetry as 'unverified' and emit an alert so security/ops can triage.

ben: dedicated pools: sometimes there is no external customer id (internal-only). we should support a manifest-level identity mapping that is explicit and audited.

marcus: manifest example allowed:

```
manifest:
  identity_translation:
    - from: external_customer_id
      to: internal_account
      audit: true
```

sophia: rate limiting placement is another cross-cutting concern. If control-plane labels but enforcement is at runtime, counters can diverge. ideas?

priya: introduce a token-lease API: control-plane mints a short-lived "rate token" with capacity & expiry. runtime consumes tokens and reports back usage asynchronously. helps avoid strong coordination while keeping safety.

ben: token-lease adds a round trip but we can gate it per-route (burst-sensitive routes default on). we should document expected latencies and opt-out controls.

marcus: action items:
- define X-Policy-* header spec, signature algorithm, and failure codes
- write cert lifecycle + provisioning doc for private/dedicated
- build token-lease prototype in control-plane
- telemetry flag for unverified hops + alerting playbook

sophia: i'll draft RFC follow-up with header spec, error mappings, and failure semantics. aiming for PR by EOD tomorrow. :rocket:

ops-bot: heads-up: canary deploy planned to dedicated/region-3 on 2025-06-02T18:00:00Z — will exercise header injection path.

ben: can we add a smoke that intentionally corrupts X-Policy-Signature so we validate 'unverified' telemetry flows?

priya: yes, add e2e test in infra that toggles cert push and asserts telemetry flags + alerting.

marcus: thanks — i'll sync with infra tomorrow to scope prototype and confirm opt-in manifest semantics.
